title: Policy and Exceptions
summary: Separate source-of-record policy text from tempting secondary notes and stale fragments.
learnerGoal: Build the smallest sufficient package for an HR policy explanation request.
taskAudience: Employee asking about vacation carryover in plain language
whyMatters: A polished answer is not enough if it uses stale policy or misses the approved exception path.
taskBrief: Answer whether the employee can carry over unused vacation hours. Use only approved HR evidence, explain any applicable exception, avoid legal advice, and say when HR review is required.
successCriteria: Uses current HR policy as the source of record.
Handles the approved exception correctly if it applies.
Avoids relying on old email summaries or training slides.
Keeps the package reviewable and within budget.
quickPredictionPrompt: Which two cards feel most tempting to include first, and why?
dynamicFacts: Manager-approved leave request was submitted before year-end.
outputContract: Return sections: Explanation / Next Steps / What We Know
Use plain language for an employee audience

cards.title: HR Policy 2026 §4.2 Carryover Rule
cards.excerpt: Unused vacation may not be carried over unless an approved exception applies. Approved exceptions require documented manager approval before year-end and HR confirmation.
cards.summaryText: Current source-of-record carryover rule with exception conditions.

cards.title: HR Exception Memo — Approved Leave Already Filed
cards.excerpt: If a leave request was approved before year-end and could not be taken, carryover may be permitted after HR confirmation.
cards.summaryText: Current approved exception path for pre-filed leave requests.

cards.title: Benefits FAQ Summary
cards.excerpt: Employees often ask whether unused vacation automatically carries over. The FAQ restates the policy in simpler language but omits the full exception logic.
cards.summaryText: Useful plain-language restatement, but redundant as direct evidence.

cards.title: 2024 Manager Email About Carryover
cards.excerpt: A manager wrote that teams were informally allowed to carry over unused hours last year while staffing was tight.

cards.title: HR Training Deck Slide
cards.excerpt: Slide says carryover is usually not allowed, with bullets that mirror older training language but not the newest exception wording.
cards.summaryText: Background-only training language; not needed verbatim.

cards.title: Union Exception Appendix
cards.excerpt: Separate rules apply for union-covered employees in a narrow bargaining unit. This employee is not marked as union-covered in the request facts.
cards.summaryText: Keep available for conditional follow-up, not core inclusion.

cards.title: Employee Record Snippet
cards.excerpt: Employee has 24 unused hours and an approved leave request filed before year-end.
cards.summaryText: Current case-specific facts needed to apply the exception.

cards.title: General Benefits Brochure
cards.excerpt: Broad overview of PTO, wellness, and family benefits. Vacation carryover is mentioned only at a high level.
cards.summaryText: Background brochure not needed for this answer.

cards.title: HR Escalation Guidance
cards.excerpt: If policy language is silent or a case falls outside the approved exception path, instruct the employee to contact HR for review.
cards.summaryText: Useful fallback instruction, but can stay deferred unless uncertainty appears.

commentary: Directly include the source-of-record policy, the applicable exception memo, and the case facts.
Summarize helpful restatements instead of pasting them verbatim.
Keep narrow edge-case material available through Retrieve Later rather than crowding the main package.
Omit stale or brochure-style background that does not materially improve the answer.

bonusBranches.title: Stricter Budget Replay
bonusBranches.description: Replay the same mission with a tighter budget to expose what really deserves entry.
bonusBranches.coachNote: Protect the policy rule, approved exception, and employee record first. Everything else must justify its footprint.

overlayCards.title: Case Header — Exception Review Intake
overlayCards.excerpt: Reviewer needs a short answer grounded in the current carryover rule, the documented exception path, and the employee record only.
overlayCards.summaryText: Compact case frame for the tighter-budget replay.

commentary: The stricter-budget replay should protect only the few cards that directly change the answer.
Compact replay-only constraint cards can shape the answer without demanding another full direct include.
Older background and follow-up material should move into Summarize, Retrieve Later, or Omit much earlier than in the core run.

bonusBranches.title: Authority vs Freshness Drill
bonusBranches.description: Re-run the case while explicitly resisting stale manager guidance when current HR policy and exception records are available.
bonusBranches.coachNote: Treat current HR policy and current exception evidence as the spine. Do not let stale manager email guidance outrank source-of-record material.

overlayCards.title: HR Queue Snapshot — Today
overlayCards.excerpt: Current HR queue notes show the case is being reviewed through the approved-exception path. Stale manager guidance should not determine the answer.
overlayCards.summaryText: Fresh source-of-record note for the authority-versus-freshness replay.

commentary: The authority-versus-freshness replay should make current source-of-record evidence visibly lead the answer.
Branch-only fresh evidence should change what the best package looks like, not just how the coaching sounds.
Comfortable but aging summaries can support the answer, but they should not steer it.

pastebackAssertions.label: Carryover depends on an approved exception path
Approved leave request before year-end supports the exception
positivePhrases: approved leave request filed before year-end

pastebackAssertions.label: The answer should preserve the 24 unused hours fact when summarizing the case

factChecks.label: The case still involves 24 unused vacation hours
The approved leave request happened before year-end
The case timing remains in March 2026 when summarizing the request context

requiredCaveats.label: The answer should make HR review or confirmation explicit

compoundChecks.label: Exception path stays bounded by before-year-end approval, 24 unused hours, and HR confirmation
compoundChecks.teachingNote: This case is only safe when the approval timing, the case facts, and the HR-confirmation caveat stay connected in the same answer region.

reviewCoaching.message: Do not turn a bounded HR exception into automatic carryover. Keep the exception path explicit.
HR confirmation is part of the answer logic here, not optional follow-up decoration.
Approval timing, the 24-hour case fact, and HR confirmation should stay connected in the same answer region.
